title: Portraits Through Time
description: Faces that have held our gaze across the centuries.
source: Art Institute of Chicago, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Wikimedia Commons

items.title: Portrait of an Artist
items.description_narrative: This 1644 oil on canvas, titled 'Portrait of an Artist,' captures a figure characteristic of 17th-century European portraiture. Attributed to a follower of Frans Hals, it exemplifies the detailed yet lively brushwork often associated with the Dutch Golden Age.
items.tags: portrait, oil painting, 17th century, dutch golden age, baroque, frans hals follower, european art
items.credit_line: https://www.artic.edu/artworks/862

items.title: The Captive Slave (Ira Aldridge)
items.description_narrative: This 1827 oil on canvas by John Philip Simpson portrays Ira Aldridge, an African American actor, in a poignant dramatic role as a captive slave. The artwork captures a moment of intense emotion, reflecting themes of bondage and human dignity.
items.tags: portrait, slavery, Ira Aldridge, acting, oil painting, 19th century, dramatic, realism
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Portrait of a Man with Gray Hair
items.description_narrative: Sir Henry Raeburn's "Portrait of a Man with Gray Hair" exemplifies the artist's masterful use of oil on canvas to capture individual character. This work showcases Raeburn's distinctive style, focusing on the sitter's presence and the subtle play of light and shadow.
items.tags: portrait, man, georgian, scottish, oil painting, realism, dignified
items.credit_line: https://www.artic.edu/artworks/15708

items.title: Édouard Manet
items.description_narrative: Henri Fantin-Latour's 1867 oil portrait captures Édouard Manet, a pivotal figure in 19th-century French art, with a direct and contemplative gaze. This work exemplifies Fantin-Latour's skill in intimate portraiture, rendering a fellow artist with notable realism and psychological depth.
items.tags: portrait, oil painting, 19th century, french art, realism, artist portrait, contemplative
items.credit_line: https://www.artic.edu/artworks/87467

items.title: Madame de Pastoret and Her Son
items.description_narrative: Jacques Louis David's unfinished portrait from 1791–92 captures Madame de Pastoret and her son in a composition characteristic of Neoclassical elegance. The work reveals a tender maternal bond, presented with a formal yet intimate gaze typical of French portraiture of the late 18th century.
items.tags: portrait, neoclassical, mother and child, family, French art, 18th century, tenderness, oil painting
items.credit_line: https://www.artic.edu/artworks/27307

items.title: Old Man with a Gold Chain
items.description_narrative: Rembrandt van Rijn’s 1631 oil on panel portrays an elderly man, his face illuminated and meticulously rendered. A prominent gold chain adorns his neck, highlighting the subject's status or wealth.
items.tags: portrait, oil painting, old man, dutch golden age, realism, baroque, dignified
items.credit_line: FAEStDTOypM-CQ at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Young Woman at an Open Half-Door
items.description_narrative: This oil on canvas depicts a young woman standing at an open half-door, illuminated by light. Created in 1645 by the Workshop of Rembrandt van Rijn, it showcases the characteristic use of light and shadow.
items.tags: young woman, portrait, doorway, dutch golden age, baroque, figure study, oil painting
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: The Child's Bath
items.description_narrative: Mary Cassatt's 'The Child's Bath' captures a tender moment of a woman bathing a young child, emphasizing the intimacy and routine of domestic life. Through soft colors and a close perspective, Cassatt highlights the emotional bond and quiet dignity of her subjects.
items.tags: mother and child, domestic scene, impressionism, american art, 19th century, oil painting, intimacy, everyday life
items.credit_line: Google Arts & Culture: Home page – Image

items.title: Interrupted Reading
items.medium: Oil on canvas, mounted on board
items.description_narrative: Jean-Baptiste-Camille Corot's 'Interrupted Reading' depicts a woman, engrossed in a book, momentarily looking up from her pages. This intimate figure study exemplifies Corot's characteristic blend of natural observation and poetic serenity, inviting quiet contemplation.
items.tags: figure study, reading, woman, contemplative, realism, barbizon school, 19th century art, interior scene
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Madame François Buron
items.description_narrative: This early work by Jacques Louis David portrays Madame François Buron, executed in oil on canvas. The painting showcases the emerging talent of a master who would soon redefine French art.
items.tags: portraiture, 18th century, french art, oil painting, david, pre-neoclassical
items.credit_line: https://www.artic.edu/artworks/88632

items.title: Portrait of a Man with a Pink
items.description_narrative: Quentin Massys's oil on panel portrait features a man holding a pink flower, rendered with precise detail characteristic of the artist's style. This work exemplifies early 16th-century Netherlandish portraiture, capturing the subject's gaze and individual features.
items.tags: portrait, man, flower, early netherlandish, renaissance, flemish, oil painting, detailed
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Amédée-David, the Comte de Pastoret
items.description_narrative: Jean Auguste Dominique Ingres masterfully captures Amédée-David, the Comte de Pastoret, in this oil on canvas. The portrait exemplifies Ingres's Neoclassical precision and refined brushwork, emphasizing the subject's dignified presence.
items.tags: portrait, neoclassicism, french art, 19th century, oil painting, male portrait, formality, academic art
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Merahi metua no Tehamana (Tehamana Has Many Parents or The Ancestors of Tehamana)
items.description_narrative: This portrait depicts Tehamana, a young Tahitian woman, adorned with traditional Tahitian and European elements, reflecting Gauguin's fascination with Polynesian culture. The work utilizes flattened forms and bold outlines, characteristic of the artist's Post-Impressionist style.
items.tags: tahitian, portrait, woman, post-impressionism, symbolism, exoticism, spirituality, serene
items.credit_line: sAFwO-4unkAuvw at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Francesco de' Medici
items.description_narrative: This portrait depicts Francesco de' Medici, a significant figure in Florentine history, painted by Alessandro Allori. Created around 1560, the oil on panel work reflects the elegant and formal portraiture of the late Renaissance period.
items.tags: portrait, Florentine, noble, Medici, Renaissance, Mannerism, formal, oil painting
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Beggar with Oysters (Philosopher)
items.description_narrative: This portrait depicts a figure, often identified as a philosopher or beggar, engaged with a meal of oysters. Manet's brushwork and direct gaze challenge traditional academic painting, reflecting everyday life.
items.tags: beggar, philosopher, realism, modern art, portrait, oysters, 19th century
items.credit_line: https://www.artic.edu/artworks/8969

items.title: Polynesian Woman with Children
items.description_narrative: Paul Gauguin's oil on linen canvas depicts a Polynesian woman surrounded by children, set against a vibrant tropical landscape. Painted in 1901, this work exemplifies Gauguin's distinctive use of bold colors and simplified forms to portray scenes of Tahitian life.
items.tags: polynesian, woman, children, tahiti, post-impressionism, symbolism, tropical, landscape
items.credit_line: Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Portrait of General José Manuel Romero
items.agent_name: Francisco José de Goya y Lucientes
items.description_narrative: This oil on canvas, painted by Francisco José de Goya y Lucientes around 1810, depicts General José Manuel Romero. Goya, a prominent Spanish master, captures the military figure with a powerful and direct gaze.
items.tags: portrait, general, military, oil painting, goya, spanish art, 19th century
items.credit_line: https://www.artic.edu/artworks/89043

items.title: Portrait of Constance Pipelet
items.description_narrative: This 1797 oil on canvas depicts Constance Pipelet with a direct gaze, reflecting the portraiture styles of the late 18th century. The artist, Jean Baptiste François Désoria, captures her likeness with precise detail and a refined palette.
items.tags: portrait, oil painting, 18th century, French, woman, historical, realism
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Mrs. Potter Palmer
items.description_narrative: This striking oil on canvas portrait depicts Mrs. Potter Palmer, rendered with Anders Zorn's characteristic skill in capturing the vitality of his sitters. Created in 1893, the work showcases Zorn's mastery of brushwork and his ability to convey both elegance and presence.
items.tags: portrait, woman, oil painting, realism, elegant, late 19th century, Swedish art, impressionistic brushwork
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: John Thomlinson and His Family
items.description_narrative: This oil on canvas painting by Arthur Devis depicts John Thomlinson and his family. Created in 1745, it captures a family group in a domestic setting.
items.tags: portrait, family, group portrait, oil painting, 18th century, British, domestic scene
items.credit_line: https://www.artic.edu/artworks/2169

items.title: Portrait of a Noblewoman Dressed in Mourning
items.description_narrative: This striking oil on canvas by Jacopo da Empoli depicts a noblewoman draped in black, her somber attire signifying a period of mourning. Created around 1600, the portrait captures a sense of quiet dignity and personal loss.
items.tags: portrait, noblewoman, mourning, Baroque, Italian, oil painting, grief, somber
items.credit_line: https://www.artic.edu/artworks/11390

items.title: Helena Tromper Du Bois
items.description_narrative: This oil on canvas depicts Helena Tromper Du Bois, a subject of Anthony van Dyck's brush. Van Dyck, celebrated for his elegant portraits, masterfully captured the likeness and status of his sitters during the Baroque era.
items.tags: portrait, flemish, baroque, woman, elegance, 17th century
items.credit_line: https://www.artic.edu/artworks/866

items.title: Self-Portrait
items.description_narrative: Frédéric Bazille captures his own likeness in this introspective oil on canvas, completed during a pivotal period in his early career. The direct gaze and naturalistic rendering reflect the artistic innovations emerging in mid-19th century France.
items.tags: self-portrait, male, artist, 19th century, oil painting, early impressionism, france, naturalism
items.credit_line: https://www.artic.edu/artworks/110661

items.title: Portrait of a Woman with a Man at a Casement
items.description_narrative: Fra Filippo Lippi masterfully painted this tempera on wood, depicting a prominent woman with a man in the background. Titled "Portrait of a Woman with a Man at a Casement," this artwork presents two figures positioned near a window.
items.tags: portrait, woman, man, tempera, Renaissance, Italian, figural
items.credit_line: Collection of The Metropolitan Museum of Art

items.title: Portrait of Doge Leonardo Loredan
items.description_narrative: Venice's newly elected Doge is rendered in his gold-brocaded ceremonial cap and mantle with a stillness and precision that recalls Netherlandish portraiture. Bellini's crisp modeling of light on fabric and flesh set a new standard for Venetian state portraiture.
items.tags: renaissance, portrait, venetian, ceremonial, dignified, bellini, doge
items.credit_line: National Gallery, London

items.title: Portrait of Baldassare Castiglione
items.description_narrative: The author of The Book of the Courtier gazes calmly out in soft grays and blacks, his intelligent, composed expression matching the ideal of courtly refinement he wrote about. Raphael's muted palette and psychological restraint influenced generations of portraitists, including Rembrandt.
items.tags: renaissance, portrait, italian, refined, understated, raphael, courtier
items.credit_line: Staatliche Museen zu Berlin

items.title: The Ambassadors
items.description_narrative: Two richly dressed French envoys stand beside a table of scientific and musical instruments, with a wildly distorted skull stretched across the foreground floor as a memento mori visible only from an oblique angle. Holbein's technical virtuosity turns a diplomatic portrait into an elaborate meditation on mortality and knowledge.
items.tags: renaissance, portrait, german, anamorphic, symbolic, holbein, memento mori
items.credit_line: Google Arts & Culture — bQEWbLB26MG1LA

items.title: Portrait of Henry VIII
items.description_narrative: The English king stands in a wide, imposing stance, his broad shoulders and jeweled costume filling the panel with an aura of absolute authority. Holbein's court portrait became the definitive visual image of Henry VIII, endlessly copied throughout the Tudor era.
items.tags: renaissance, portrait, royal, german, imposing, holbein, tudor
items.credit_line: Own work

items.title: Portrait of a Man in a Red Turban
items.description_narrative: A man in an elaborately folded red chaperon meets the viewer's gaze directly against a plain dark ground, possibly a self-portrait of the artist. Van Eyck's precise inscription and virtuoso rendering of cloth and stubble mark one of the earliest true self-portraits in Western painting.
items.tags: renaissance, portrait, flemish, precise, early, van eyck, self-portrait
items.credit_line: EXTRACTED (AND COMPRESSED) FROM AN OLD VERSION OF THIS FILE File:Portrait of a Man by Jan van Eyck.jpg.

items.title: The Arnolfini Portrait
items.description_narrative: A merchant and his wife stand hand in hand in a richly furnished chamber, a convex mirror on the back wall reflecting the room and two additional figures in the doorway. Dense with symbolic detail, from the single candle to the small dog, it remains one of the most scrutinized domestic portraits ever painted.
items.tags: renaissance, portrait, flemish, symbolic, domestic, van eyck, double portrait
items.credit_line: Web site of National Gallery, London

items.title: Infanta Margarita Teresa in a Blue Dress
items.description_narrative: The young Spanish princess stands stiffly in an enormous silver-blue gown, her small figure nearly swallowed by court fashion and formal etiquette. Velázquez's loose, atmospheric brushwork on the fabric contrasts with the child's composed, direct gaze.
items.tags: baroque, portrait, spanish, royal, court, velazquez, childhood
items.credit_line: pAHSoRgE1VSx2w at Google Cultural Institute maximum zoom level

items.title: Charles I at the Hunt
items.cultural_context: Flemish Baroque at the English court
items.description_narrative: Van Dyck presents King Charles I informally at rest during a hunt, one hand on a cane, as a courtier holds his horse. The low viewpoint and elegant pose lend an air of effortless majesty to the notably short monarch.
items.credit_line: https://www.picassozx.com/content/?11905.html

items.title: Portrait of Pope Innocent X
items.description_narrative: Painted during Velazquez's second stay in Italy, this portrait fixes the pope with an unflinching, penetrating realism that the sitter himself reportedly found too truthful. Widely counted among the greatest portraits ever made, it later obsessed the painter Francis Bacon.
items.credit_line: http://picasaweb.google.com/EnrikeCdC/VelazquezObraCompleta#5297131513290212530

items.title: Portrait of Pope Julius II
items.description_narrative: Raphael broke with convention by showing the pope seated and inwardly absorbed rather than in rigid formal majesty, setting the template for papal portraiture for two centuries. The unusual beard was grown by Julius as a vow tied to the fortunes of the papal states.
items.credit_line: Google Arts & Culture — TAEKLWNeHElstQ

items.title: Self-Portrait in a Straw Hat
items.description_narrative: The artist depicts herself outdoors with a palette in hand and a feathered straw hat, directly inspired by a Rubens portrait she had admired in Antwerp. Her unpowdered hair and natural presentation were a fresh, informal statement in the years just before the Revolution.
items.credit_line: Selected work 27 from Self Portrait: Renaissance to Contemporary (Anthony Bond, Joanna Woodall, ISBN 978-1855143579).

items.title: Alexander Grant
items.description_narrative: Scottish-born portraitist Cosmo Alexander painted this likeness of Alexander Grant while working as an itinerant painter in Britain's American colonies. Alexander is historically notable as an early teacher of the young Gilbert Stuart, who became America's foremost portraitist.
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Lucrezia di Lippo di Iacopo Guidi
items.description_narrative: Andrea del Sarto, one of the leading painters of the High Renaissance in Florence, painted this pendant portrait of a Florentine woman alongside a companion portrait of her husband. The sitter's identity and social standing are conveyed through the careful rendering of her dress and composed bearing.
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Portrait of Dr. William McNeill Whistler
items.description_narrative: James McNeill Whistler painted this portrait of his half-brother, William McNeill Whistler, a physician who served as a Confederate surgeon during the American Civil War. The restrained palette and tonal harmony reflect Whistler's mature aesthetic philosophy of 'art for art's sake.'
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Arrangement in Flesh Color and Brown: Portrait of Arthur Jerome Eddy
items.description_narrative: This striking oil portrait, titled "Arrangement in Flesh Color and Brown," captures Arthur Jerome Eddy with an emphasis on color harmony rather than detailed representation. Created by James McNeill Whistler in 1894, it exemplifies his innovative approach to portraiture as a study in tonal relationships and artistic arrangement.
items.tags: portrait, oil painting, whistler, tonalism, aestheticism, fin de siècle, american art
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Mrs. John Nicholson (Hannah Duncan) and John Nicholson, Jr.
items.description_narrative: This double portrait by Charles Willson Peale depicts Hannah Duncan Nicholson and her son, John Nicholson, Jr., capturing a tender familial moment. Painted in oil on canvas in 1790, it exemplifies Peale's skill in rendering lifelike figures and intimate domestic scenes.
items.tags: portrait, mother and child, family, 18th century, american art, oil painting, realism, domestic scene
items.credit_line: https://www.artic.edu/artworks/78507

items.title: James Vibert, Sculptor
items.description_narrative: Ferdinand Hodler's 1907 oil on canvas presents a portrait titled 'James Vibert, Sculptor'. The painting depicts the sculptor James Vibert, created by Hodler, and serves as an example of his portraiture.
items.tags: portraiture, male subject, sculptor, oil painting, 1907, ferdinand hodler
items.credit_line: https://www.artic.edu/artworks/27962

items.title: James William Wallack
items.description_narrative: This oil on canvas painting by Charles Robert Leslie depicts James William Wallack. Created between 1835 and 1840, it showcases Leslie's skill as a portraitist.
items.tags: portrait, oil painting, 19th century, male figure, charles robert leslie, james william wallack, american art, british art
items.credit_line: https://www.artic.edu/artworks/8475

items.title: Isabella Wolff
items.description_narrative: Sir Thomas Lawrence's oil on canvas portrait depicts Isabella Wolff, capturing her refined presence with remarkable detail. Created between 1803 and 1815, this work exemplifies the artist's celebrated ability to convey character and elegance through his brushwork.
items.tags: portrait, woman, romanticism, british art, oil painting, 19th century, elegance, refined
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Dr. Joseph Klapp
items.description_narrative: Painted by Thomas Sully in 1814, this oil on canvas depicts Dr. Joseph Klapp. The work serves as a formal portrait, representative of American painting from the early 19th century.
items.tags: portrait, oil painting, American, 19th century, formal, doctor, realism
items.credit_line: https://www.artic.edu/artworks/96621

items.title: Mrs. Klapp (Anna Milnor)
items.description_narrative: Thomas Sully's 1814 oil on canvas presents a portrait of Mrs. Klapp, also known as Anna Milnor. This work exemplifies the artist's refined approach to capturing individual likeness through the medium of paint.
items.tags: portrait, oil painting, American art, 19th century, realism, woman, Thomas Sully
items.credit_line: https://www.artic.edu/artworks/72375

items.title: Sarah Dupont
items.description_narrative: Thomas Gainsborough was a prominent English portrait and landscape painter of the 18th century. This oil painting captures a likeness, reflecting the artist's characteristic elegant style and mastery of brushwork.
items.tags: portraiture, 18th century, British art, oil painting, elegant, aristocratic, Georgian era
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Riter Fitzgerald
items.description_narrative: Thomas Eakins's 1895 portrait of Riter Fitzgerald exemplifies his commitment to capturing individual presence rather than idealizing his subjects. Through a muted palette and direct gaze, Eakins reveals a quiet intensity in the sitter.
items.tags: portrait, american realism, oil painting, male subject, 19th century, psychological, muted
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Portrait of Mary Adeline Williams
items.description_narrative: Thomas Eakins's 1899 oil on canvas depicts Mary Adeline Williams with a characteristic directness and psychological insight. His work is celebrated for its unvarnished realism, capturing the sitter's individual presence with a precise eye.
items.tags: portrait, realism, american art, oil painting, late 19th century, psychological, contemplative
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Rêverie (Portrait of Gabrielle Borreau)
items.medium: Oil on paper, mounted on canvas
items.description_narrative: This intimate portrait by Gustave Courbet depicts Gabrielle Borreau in a contemplative pose. Painted in 1862, the work captures a moment of quiet introspection.
items.tags: portrait, realism, 19th century, contemplative, figure study, oil painting, french art
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago

items.title: Mère Grégoire
items.description_narrative: Gustave Courbet's 'Mère Grégoire' is an oil on canvas portrait depicting an older woman. This work exemplifies Courbet's commitment to portraying everyday people with directness and realism.
items.tags: portrait, woman, realism, french realism, direct, naturalistic, oil painting
items.credit_line: Collection of Art Institute of Chicago
